skill.name: ci
skill.description: Analyzes CI/CD failures, reviews build and test logs, and guides safe fixes for failed pipeline jobs.
skill.summary: Diagnose CI failures and guide safe build or test fixes.
skill.author: Chachamaru127

security_audit.summary: The static backtick and entropy alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code, Japanese text, and diagrams. I found one medium semantic issue: shell examples interpolate run IDs and test paths without validation or quoting. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Unvalidated command placeholders in Bash examples.
remediation.suggestion: Require numeric run_id values, quote file path arguments, reject shell metacharacters, and prefer structured tool arguments over interpolated Bash.

remediation.issue: Command examples can contact GitHub or execute project tests.
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to explain the command first and ask before running commands that use credentials, CI logs, or repository state.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Shell Command Placeholders
semantic_findings.description: Several Bash examples interpolate run IDs and test file paths as placeholders without stating validation or quoting requirements. A malicious value could alter the intended command if copied directly into a shell.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command templates contain user-provided placeholders in Bash examples. The skill context is legitimate CI work, so confidence is high enough to remediate but not a critical intent finding.

content.user_title: Diagnose CI Failures and Fix Tests
content.value_statement: CI failures waste time when logs are noisy and causes are unclear. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code triage pipeline failures and guide safe fixes.
actual_capabilities: Classifies CI failures as build, test, dependency, or environment issues.
Guides review of GitHub Actions logs with GitHub CLI examples.
Suggests safe fixes for failing tests and implementation defects.
Discourages test skipping, assertion removal, and CI bypasses.
Provides report templates for analysis results and fix summaries.
Escalates complex repeated failures to a CI fixer subagent pattern.
limitations: Requires repository context and CI logs to produce useful guidance.
Does not guarantee that suggested fixes will pass every pipeline.
Bash examples should be reviewed before execution in sensitive repositories.
Focused on CI failures, not general feature development or code review.

use_cases.title: Triage a Failed Pipeline
use_cases.description: Identify the likely failure class and the first file or job to inspect.

use_cases.title: Repair Failing Tests
use_cases.description: Compare test expectations with implementation behavior and choose a safe fix.

use_cases.title: Prepare a CI Incident Summary
use_cases.description: Create a concise report with cause, affected files, fix status, and next actions.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One Failure
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a single failed job.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this CI failure log. Identify the error type, likely cause, related files, and the safest next action.

prompt_templates.title: Find the Root Cause
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the failed CI job and recent commits. Explain which change most likely caused the failure and why.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Failing Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced repair with test and implementation context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fix this failing test without weakening coverage. Decide whether the test or implementation is wrong, then apply the smallest correct change.

prompt_templates.title: Stabilize Repeated Failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for repeated CI failures.
prompt_templates.prompt: The same CI job failed after two fix attempts. Diagnose the loop, propose a safer plan, and list commands that need approval before running.

output_examples.input: The build job fails with a TypeScript error after the latest commit.
output_examples.output: The result identifies a build failure, points to the likely changed file, explains the type mismatch, and recommends fixing implementation types first.

output_examples.input: A Vitest assertion fails because the received value changed.
output_examples.output: The result compares the expected behavior with the implementation, recommends the correct owner of the fix, and avoids removing assertions.

output_examples.input: The CI fix has failed twice and affects several files.
output_examples.output: The result summarizes the repeated failure pattern, separates environment risk from code risk, and proposes an approval-based retry plan.

best_practices: Provide the failed job log, run ID, and recent commit context together.
Fix implementation defects before changing tests or CI settings.
Review Bash commands before running them with repository credentials.
anti_patterns: Do not skip tests to make CI pass without a documented temporary reason.
Do not remove assertions unless the requirement has changed.
Do not add CI bypass settings instead of fixing the root cause.

faq.question: What CI systems does this skill support?
faq.answer: It focuses on general CI patterns and includes GitHub Actions examples. The same triage flow can help with other systems.

faq.question: Can it run CI commands automatically?
faq.answer: It provides command examples, but users should approve commands that access logs, credentials, or repository state.

faq.question: Will it modify tests?
faq.answer: It can guide test changes when the test is wrong. It prefers implementation fixes when behavior is incorrect.

faq.question: Does it allow skipping tests?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly discourages permanent skips, deleted assertions, and CI bypasses.

faq.question: What input gives the best result?
faq.answer: Provide the failed job name, relevant log section, run ID, recent changes, and affected test files.

faq.question: Is this useful for local build failures?
faq.answer: It is designed for CI failures. Local builds may need a more general debugging workflow.
